sections.title: Onboarding Process via EOR in Comoros

steps.title: Contract Drafting and Legal Review
steps.description: Drafting the 'Indefinite-Term' or 'Fixed-Term' contract in French. Articles must comply with the 2008 Labor Code, specifically detailing job roles, 40-hour work week, and compensation in KMF.

steps.title: Mandatory Medical Fitness Certification
steps.description: New hires must undergo a medical examination at an authorized healthcare facility. A fitness certificate is legally required before the employee can formally start their duties.

steps.title: Labor Inspectorate Notification
steps.description: Notifying the local Labor Inspectorate (Inspection du Travail) of the new hire to ensure registration in the national workforce database.

steps.title: Social Security (CNPS) Enrollment
steps.description: The EOR registers the employee with the Caisse Nationale de Prévoyance Sociale (CNPS). Both employer and employee contributions (totaling 11%+) are set up for monthly filing.

items.title: Standard Work Week
items.text: The statutory work week in Comoros is 40 hours. Any work beyond this must be compensated at tired overtime rates (15%, 30%, 40%).

items.title: Probation Period Norms
items.text: Probation is typically 1 to 3 months for non-executives and up to 6 months for management, allowing both parties to assess the fit.

items.title: Strict Termination Laws
items.text: Terminating an indefinite contract (CDI) requires 'just cause' and adherence to strict notice periods (usually 1 month) to avoid costly labor tribunal disputes.

faqs.question: Can I hire foreign nationals via EOR in Comoros?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they require a valid work permit and residence visa. The EOR manages the application process with the Ministry of the Interior and Labor, ensuring all immigration laws are strictly followed.

faqs.question: Who is the legal employer of record?
faqs.answer: The EOR entity is the legal employer, assuming all payroll and compliance liabilities, while the client manages the employee's daily tasks and deliverables.

faqs.question: How is payroll funded?
faqs.answer: Clients typically pre-fund payroll in USD or EUR, which the EOR converts to Comorian Francs (KMF) for distribution to staff, protecting you from local currency volatility.

faqs.question: What happens if a labor dispute arises?
faqs.answer: The EOR manages the legal representation and mediation at the local Labor Tribunal (Tribunal du Travail) on your behalf.

items.title: Annual Paid Leave
items.description: Employees are legally entitled to 2 days of paid leave per month worked, totaling 24 days per calendar year.

items.title: Maternity Protection
items.description: Pregnant employees receive 14 weeks of maternity leave, typically paid at 100% of their salary through a combination of CNPS and employer contribution.

items.title: Sick Leave Provisions
items.description: Up to 6 months of paid sick leave may be granted, supported by a certified medical practitioner's report.

items.title: Bilingualism in the Workplace
items.text: While French is the language of administration, using Comorian (Shicomori) in casual workplace interactions significantly enhances team cohesion.

items.title: Prayer Break Accommodations
items.text: Given the majority Muslim population, allowing brief breaks for daily prayers is a standard practice and respected by employers.

items.title: Friday Early Close
items.text: Many offices in Moroni close early on Friday afternoons for Jumu'ah prayers; scheduling meetings before noon is advised.

steps.title: Monthly Data Collection
steps.description: Aggregating fixed salaries, overtime hours (at 15/30/40% tiers), and any performance-based bonuses or housing allowances.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculations
steps.description: Processing statutory deductions: 4% to 6% employee CNPS and progressive IRPP tax (0% to 30% depending on income brackets).

steps.title: Statutory Payment Remittance
steps.description: Transferring withheld taxes to the DGI and social security contributions to the CNPS by the 15th of the following month.

steps.title: Digital Payslip Distribution
steps.description: Issuing French-language payslips to employees via secure portals, ensuring transparency in all earnings and deductions.

items.title: SMIG Benchmark 2025
items.text: The national minimum wage (SMIG) is strictly set at 55,000 KMF per month. All full-time contracts must meet or exceed this floor.

items.title: KMF-EUR Peg Benefits
items.text: Since the Comorian Franc (KMF) is pegged to the Euro, payroll costs remain relatively stable for European-based corporate HQs.

items.title: Cash Payment Risks
items.text: While common in local markets, international compliance requires bank transfers to avoid 'grey' labor pitfalls and ensure audit trails.

items.title: Employee Contract (Contrat de Travail)
items.description: A signed copy of the contract must be on file for every employee, detailing their KMF gross salary and job classification.

items.title: Social Security Card (Carte CNPS)
items.description: Mandatory for all local hires to ensure contributions are credited to the correct individual pension account.

items.title: Medical Fitness Certificate
items.description: Must be renewed annually and stored with the individual's payroll record for compliance audits.

faqs.question: Can we pay employees in USD?
faqs.answer: Legally, local employees must be paid in KMF. While contracts may reference USD benchmarks, the final payout must adhere to local currency laws.

faqs.question: What is the deadline for tax remittance?
faqs.answer: All withheld IRPP taxes must be paid to the DGI by the 15th of the month following the payroll cycle.

faqs.question: Is there a 13th-month salary requirement?
faqs.answer: No, it is not a statutory requirement in Comoros, but it is a common discretionary benefit provided by international firms during the Islamic holidays.

steps.title: Base Salary & SMIG Check
steps.description: Ensuring the base meets the statutory minimum (SMIG) of 55,000 KMF per month.

steps.title: Overtime Tiering
steps.description: Applying 15% for the first 8 hours, 30% for hours 9-16, and 40% for hours beyond 16 or holiday work.

steps.title: Statutory Deductions (CNPS)
steps.description: Subtracting the employee's mandatory social security contribution (typically 4% to 6%).

steps.title: Progressive Tax (IRPP)
steps.description: Applying the 7-tier tax brackets, starting from 0% for income under 150k KMF up to 30% for the top tier.

items.title: Exempt Tier (0%)
items.text: Income from 0 to 150,000 KMF per year is non-taxable, providing essential relief for low-wage earners.

items.title: Middle Tiers (5% - 20%)
items.text: Progressive steps occur at 500k, 1M, 1.5M, and 2.5M KMF annual income markers.

items.title: Top Tier (30%)
items.text: High earners with income exceeding 3.5M KMF are subject to the maximum rate of 30%.

items.title: Customary 13th Month
items.text: While not in the calculator's statutory logic, remember to factor in the customary 13th-month bonus when estimating annual costs.

faqs.question: Does the calculator include employer costs?
faqs.answer: The standard view shows employee take-home pay, but 'Cost to Employer' views include the 7% to 10% CNPS employer share.

faqs.question: Is the 2025 SMIG updated?
faqs.answer: Yes, the calculator uses the current 55,000 KMF SMIG benchmark for compliance checks.

faqs.question: Can it handle housing allowances?
faqs.answer: Yes, it allows for tax-free allowance inputs up to the regulatory limits defined by the Comoros Tax Code.

faqs.question: How does it calculate overtime?
faqs.answer: It applies 115% for the first 8 hours, 130% for the next 8, and 140% for any hours beyond that or on public holidays.

faqs.question: Are annual bonuses taxable?
faqs.answer: Yes, discretionary bonuses like the 13th month are usually subject to the same progressive IRPP brackets as regular salary.

faqs.question: Is Comorian salary tax-free for expats?
faqs.answer: No, non-residents are generally taxed at a flat 20% rate unless a specific bilateral tax treaty between Comoros and their home country says otherwise.

faqs.question: Does it account for family deductions?
faqs.answer: Currently, the tool uses standard brackets; however, specific child/spouse exemptions can be manually entered as tax credits.

faqs.question: How frequent are the tax logic updates?
faqs.answer: We update the calculator annually in January or whenever the DGI issues new official tax circulars.

faqs.question: Can I export the results to PDF?
faqs.answer: Yes, the 'Download Summary' feature generates a compliant breakdown of all KMF taxes and deductions in French.

faqs.question: What is the rounding logic used?
faqs.answer: All calculations are rounded up to the nearest Comorian Franc (KMF), as is standard for local payroll software.

items.title: Annual SMIG Marker
items.description: The 2025 benchmark for minimum wage is set at 660,000 KMF annually (55,000 KMF per month).

items.title: Social Security Capping
items.description: Note that CNPS contributions for certain specialized roles may be subject to monthly earnings caps, which the calculator handles automatically.

items.title: Expatriate Special Logic
items.description: Includes toggle for non-resident status, which can affect certain tax deductions and the applicability of bilateral tax treaties.

faqs.question: Can foreigners own 100% of a Comoros company?
faqs.answer: Yes, under the current investment code, foreign investors can hold 100% equity in almost all commercial sectors.

faqs.question: How long does it take to register a business?
faqs.answer: With GUFE's streamlined process, registration usually takes 7-15 business days, provided all documents are notarized correctly.

faqs.question: Are there tax incentives for new entities?
faqs.answer: Yes, investors in Free Economic Zones or specific strategic sectors (like tourism) can qualify for 5-10 year tax holidays.

faqs.question: Do I need a local physical office?
faqs.answer: Yes, a registered physical address in Comoros is mandatory for entity formation and receiving official correspondence.

faqs.question: What is the reporting currency in Comoros?
faqs.answer: Financial statements must be prepared in Comorian Francs (KMF). However, dual tracking in EUR or USD is common for international reporting packages.

faqs.question: How long should records be kept?
faqs.answer: Under OHADA regulations, all accounting books and supporting documents must be archived and available for inspection for at least 10 years.

faqs.question: Is digital signature accepted for filings?
faqs.answer: While the DGI is modernizing, many official filings still require physical 'Légalisation' stamp and wet signatures from a resident manager.

faqs.question: Can you manage our petty cash in Moroni?
faqs.answer: Yes, we provide outsourced treasury management for local operational expenses, including secure cash handling and reconciliation.

faqs.question: What is the SYSCOHADA system?
faqs.answer: It is the unified accounting system used by all OHADA member states, ensuring consistency in financial reporting across West and Central Africa.

faqs.question: Are there specialized rules for NGOs?
faqs.answer: Yes, NGOs and associations in Comoros have specific reporting requirements and different VAT treatment for grant-funded projects.

faqs.question: Can we use international auditors?
faqs.answer: Large firms often use Big Four associates, but they must be officially registered with the Comoros Order of Certified Accountants (ONCC-Comores).

faqs.question: How is depreciation handled?
faqs.answer: Depreciation rates are standardized under SYSCOHADA, with specific ranges allowed for vehicles, IT equipment, and industrial machinery.

faqs.question: Do you handle inter-company billing?
